observations: The served dependency-free page opens without browser errors online or offline, and year controls show correct district rates for 2021 and 2023.
The requested +8.0 pp Gaya and +7.0 pp Nalanda endpoint changes are correct in chat and the delivered CSV.

In the causal-caveat follow-up the agent states that the Nalanda-Gaya gap was 5.0 pp in 2022; the source values are 77.0% and 69.0%, so the correct gap is 8.0 pp. This is classified as materially_wrong_number.
The agent correctly refuses to infer why Gaya is lower and explicitly notes that this is a synthetic fixture.
The final page remains a general all-district/year dashboard; it does not show the requested Gaya/Nalanda endpoint changes or provide a comparison download button.
The delivered comparison CSV has correct 2021 and 2023 endpoints but omits the required 2022 observations and source field.
After the 2021-2023 filter, a hard-coded Gaya 2020 worked example remains visible.
The desktop design is simple, clean and legible. Its five-column table makes the narrow document 190 px wider than the 390 px viewport.

The five turns took 343.142 seconds. All 21 calls resolved to qwen/qwen3.8-27b (19 Reka, two Alibaba), cost USD 0.19939905, and used 315,293 prompt plus 16,917 completion tokens including 4,251 reasoning tokens.
evidence_notes: The score is unblinded and provisional until paired review. The wrong 2022 gap and incomplete CSV are deterministic findings.
